# Form Library Performance Comparison

Covers react-hook-form vs Formik vs React Final Form performance characteristics.
See [citations.md](../citations.md) for source details.

**Note:** No peer-reviewed academic benchmarks exist for React form library
performance. All data comes from vendor-produced benchmarks, practitioner blogs,
and community comparisons. Vendor benchmarks (especially [12]) should be treated
with appropriate skepticism.

## Bundle Size

| Library | Minified | Gzipped | Dependencies |
|---------|----------|---------|-------------|
| react-hook-form | 26.4 kb [29] | 5.2 kb [27] | 0 [27] |
| Formik | 44.4 kb [29] | 12.6 kb [27] | 9 [27] |
| React Final Form | — | 3.2-5.4 kb [46] | — |

React Final Form has the smallest bundle; react-hook-form has zero dependencies.
Formik is the largest with 9 transitive dependencies [27].

## Re-render Counts

### LogRocket Benchmark (1000-field form) [27]

| Library | Re-renders |
|---------|-----------|
| react-hook-form | 3 |
| Formik | 30+ |

### Gandi Benchmark (5-field form, typing 6 characters) [28]

| Library | Re-renders |
|---------|-----------|
| react-hook-form | 7 |
| React Final Form | 8 |
| Formik | 14 |

**Methodology:** React Profiler monitoring during keystroke events on a form
with 1 text field, 1 async select, 2 radio buttons, 1 textarea [28]. Also
measured reflows and repaints.

### Official RHF Benchmark [12]

react-hook-form ~13% faster than Formik, ~25% faster than Redux Form in
1000-field test. **Vendor-produced** — the benchmark comes from the
react-hook-form team.

## Architecture Comparison

### react-hook-form: Uncontrolled + Proxy [65]

- Uses refs instead of state for input registration [27]
- ES6 Proxy tracks which parts of formState components actually read [65]
- Lazy subscription through property access — only registers subscriptions when
  properties are accessed [65]
- formState updated in batch to minimize re-renders [65]
- Re-renders isolated to components directly tied to the changed field [27]

**Early return trap:** Components returning before accessing formState properties
fail to subscribe to updates [65].

### Formik: Controlled Components [47]

- Re-renders entire form on every field change [47]
- Every keystroke triggers full form component re-render [47]
- FastField component intended for optimization but still re-renders twice on
  any field change in some versions [47]

**Workarounds:** FastField, debounce input changes, validateOnChange: false,
internal state with onBlur propagation [47].

### React Final Form: Observer Pattern [46]

- Subscription-based form state management [46]
- Only components needing updates re-render
- Granular control over rendering based on specific events/state changes
- Form component renders once; Field components render independently
- Selective subscription: `subscription={{ values: false }}` prevents
  re-renders on value changes [46]

## Performance Implications of RHF APIs

| API | Re-render Scope | When to Use |
|-----|----------------|-------------|
| `register` | None (uncontrolled) | Native HTML inputs [6] |
| `Controller` | Component level | External controlled components (MUI, etc.) [11] |
| `useWatch` | Component level [8] | Reactive field dependencies |
| `watch` | Root/form level [9] | Avoid in large forms |
| `getValues` | None (no re-render) | One-time value reads [32] |

**Best practice:** Always prefer `useWatch` over `watch` for large forms [32].
Performance difference is insignificant in small forms but clearly noticeable in
large forms with complex inputs [32].

## Deeply Nested Forms

Limited quantitative data available:
- Forms with >100 fields show significant slowdown across all libraries [46]
- React Final Form: 10+ seconds initial render reported with large arrays and
  nested subforms [46]
- No specific benchmarks for 10+ nesting levels or 50+ fields in React
  libraries

## Gaps and Limitations

- No peer-reviewed academic studies on form library performance
- Most benchmarks from library maintainers or practitioner blogs — potential bias
- Limited data on deeply nested forms (10+ levels, 50+ fields)
- No standardized benchmark methodology across different sources
- No production performance data from actual applications at scale
- React Final Form appears unmaintained — npm page shows reduced activity [46]
